text:
alex: Customer (internal ticket #5482) reports mid-stream SSE disconnects when switching from mobile data -> phone hotspot. They see a partial JSON payload (ends mid-object) and client never gets the final event. Customer says billing charged for full response though only partial bytes received.

priya: Can you paste the client logs + exact repro steps? sounds like a midstream TCP reset or proxy tear-down. :thinking_face: 

alex: Repro steps from customer: 1) Start generation via SDK with streaming enabled 2) After ~4s flip from LTE to phone-hotspot 3) client logs show SSE stalled then stream closes, final event missing. They provided this minimal curl repro: 

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2","input":"long prompt"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream
```

and a trimmed client log: 
```
[00:04.02] RECEIVED: data: {"delta":"Hello, worl
[00:04.12] socket: ECONNRESET
[00:04.13] socket: close
[00:04.14] client: reconnecting -> backoff 250ms
```

priya: Hmm partial chunk ending in "Hello, worl" indicates the connection closed mid-chunk, not a well-formed SSE close. Do we have any proxy logs for that request id? ask them to get X-Request-ID header from their next run.

oncall-ryan: Paging infra: I see some RST_STREAM on the edge for short-lived connections around that time window for other customers in the same region. Could be middlebox (carrier NAT) aborting long-lived client sockets when IP changes.

support-bot: :rotating_light: Escalation created: INC-2026-5482. Added oncall-ryan, priya, alex.

alex: Two immediate asks from customer: 1) Why was billing for full response when they only received partial bytes? 2) Any mitigations to avoid malformed partial outputs (client side or platform)?

priya: For billing — currently we charge by tokens generated server-side; even if the client disconnects midstream, tokens produced before the stream closed are billable. But we should confirm the exact byte/token counts. I'll check the usage logs.

oncall-ryan: Mitigations: client should implement resume/retry logic and dedupe final outputs. On the server side we can ensure the final "done" event is buffered until confirmation, but that breaks streaming latency guarantees. Short-term: suggest the customer enable a short keepalive ping every 15s and a reconnect policy that re-requests with stream offset if they persist.

alex: Customer asked for concrete patch they can apply now. I suggested: 1) add streaming SSE parser tolerant of truncated events, 2) persist partial deltas to local buffer and request final non-streamed fallback after N seconds of no progress. Example: 

```
// pseudocode: fallback after 3000ms stall
let lastEvent = Date.now();
onSSEChunk = (chunk) => { lastEvent = Date.now(); append(chunk); }
setInterval(() => {
  if (Date.now() - lastEvent > 3000) {
    // call non-stream generate API to get final content
    fetch('/v1/generate', {body: originalPayload})
  }
}, 1000)
```

priya: That's reasonable. Also flagged a request to infra to look for any edge idle timeouts or abrupt RSTs in the 1735503200-1735503600 window.

oncall-ryan: I pulled edge logs: a few proxied connections did see FIN from client side matching hotspot toggle, and one case an edge backend reported "write failed: broken pipe" immediately after a long chunk. No explicit 5xx from backend.

alex: Customer claims they saw a 502 in a different run. Could the edge translate the midstream abort to 502 for some client libraries?

oncall-ryan: Yes, some HTTP libs surface a 502 when a proxy resets the connection. We'll add a note in the docs: when switching networks mid-request, clients can observe truncated SSE or 5xx depending on middleboxes.

priya: Action items: 
- priya: confirm token count and billing for ticket INC-2026-5482 (by EOD)
- oncall-ryan: verify edge/proxy timeouts + file any infra fixes if pattern repeats (24h)
- alex: share suggested client-side fallback snippet with customer and ask for X-Request-ID + pcap if they can (privately)

alex: Customer asked if we can detect truncated JSON server-side and mark request as "incomplete" for billing refunds. Is that feasible?

oncall-ryan: Hard to correlate client disconnect vs final token emission reliably. We bill on tokens emitted by the model process. We can add a customer-facing meter that flags sessions that closed before sending a final "done" event and surface for manual refunds, but automated refunds risk abuse. I'll open a follow-up feature RFC.

priya: I'll reply to customer with the short-term checklist + client snippet + note about billing policy and that we're investigating edge resets.

support-bot: Update: INC-2026-5482 moved to "investigating".

alex: Thanks — I'll send a repro request and ask them to run with debug flags to capture X-Request-ID. If they can provide a short pcap around the network switch that would help. :pray: 

priya: One more small idea: recommend customer to set SDK option `stream_keepalive: 15s` so TCP keepalives/heartbeats are more frequent. We can add a doc snippet in the streaming troubleshooting page.

oncall-ryan: Agree. I'll also check if our load-balancer can lower idle window for affected region as an experiment.

alex: Closing loop here; will post customer response and any pcap when they attach.
